record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Can one prove that there is no counterexample (f,g) to the two-dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with f and g both lying in the subring C[Y, XY, X^2Y, X^3Y-X]?

evidence.quote: QUESTION. Can one prove there does not exist a counterexample ( f, g) to the Jacobian Conjecture such that f, g ∈ C[Y, XY, X 2Y, X 3Y − X]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The two-dimensional Jacobian Conjecture asserts that if $f,g\in\mathbb{C}[X,Y]$ satisfy $\det\begin{pmatrix}f_X & f_Y\\ g_X & g_Y\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{C}^{*}$, then the map $(X,Y)\mapsto(f(X,Y),g(X,Y))$ is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^2$ (equivalently, $\mathbb{C}[f,g]=\mathbb{C}[X,Y]$). A counterexample would be a pair $(f,g)\in\mathbb{C}[X,Y]^2$ with nonzero constant Jacobian for which $\mathbb{C}[f,g]\subsetneq\mathbb{C}[X,Y]$.

Let $R\subset\mathbb{C}[X,Y]$ denote the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra
$$R=\mathbb{C}[\,Y,\;XY,\;X^{2}Y,\;X^{3}Y-X\,].$$

Prove that there does not exist a counterexample $(f,g)$ to the two-dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with $f\in R$ and $g\in R$. That is, show that any pair $f,g\in R$ whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant must satisfy $\mathbb{C}[f,g]=\mathbb{C}[X,Y]$.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-dimensional Jacobian Conjecture remains open in general, and no published resolution of this specific restricted version (counterexamples lying in the subring C[Y, XY, X²Y, X³Y−X]) was found in the search. Recent surveys and papers (e.g., on the shape of possible counterexamples) continue to treat the Jacobian Conjecture as open, with no targeted result on this subring.
